gap: No result ChatGPT got puts the two makers' battery-life claims on the same footing: eufy rates the S330 at 'about a month' for a stated workload (10 ten-second motion events plus 5 live views a day, no solar), while Reolink rates the Go PT Ultra at 'up to two months' with no workload stated, and both cameras record only on events (Reolink leaves the Go PT Ultra off its own list of battery cameras that can record continuously). So the 2x gap on paper is not a measured difference.
standout_why: Pages compared: smarthomeexplorer.com (Oct 12, 2026), homesecurityradar.com's no-Wi-Fi guide and its data-cost guide (cited), buffaloalarm.com (cited), and reolink.com/us Go PT Ultra (cited). None gives eufy's battery-life workload or sets it beside Reolink's claim, which has no workload. Smarthomeexplorer and Buffalo Alarm list no battery-life figures. homesecurityradar's no-Wi-Fi guide lists both batteries (9,400 mAh and 21.6 Wh) but not their runtimes. Its data-cost page attaches a workload to data use (700 MB/month), not to battery life. On recording, every rival says 'not stated' or 'most record motion events'. None cites Reolink's own list of models that can record continuously. On carriers, rivals already have part of it. homesecurityradar notes that Verizon is not among Reolink's recommended plans and that the band list is the same as the S330's. Smarthomeexplorer says Reolink's SIM picks among AT&T, Verizon and T-Mobile, which goes against Reolink's own spec table (T-Mobile and AT&T prepaid only).
decides: This backs eufy S330 over Reolink Go PT Ultra for a shopper on a Verizon-only rural site. eufy names Verizon in its carrier spec. Reolink's spec table names only T-Mobile and AT&T prepaid, even though the US band lists are identical. It also means the page can't say the Reolink lasts twice as long on a charge: only eufy publishes the conditions behind its figure. For a shopper who picked '24/7 continuous recording' in ChatGPT's follow-up questions, neither of these two cameras qualifies. Both record on events.
